moves.evidence: Ming-Chi Kuo (TF International analyst; his own post, Nov 20 2026 14:55 UTC, read verbatim via the fxtwitter mirror of the post): 'Google has cut 2027 shipments of the Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by ~1M units (mostly the higher-priced 8i Max / Whalefish). The cut amounts to roughly 20% of 2027 TPU 8i series shipments' and Google 'plans to increase 2027 shipments of the MediaTek-designed TPU 8t series, though details aren't final yet', citing supply-chain and data-center power limits. An analyst's industry survey, not a Google or Broadcom statement; neither company has commented. Sizing from the item's own units: 1.0M units x $15.24k revenue per unit (the AVGO set's own Q3 FY26 XPU revenue per TPU, ~800k units for $12,191M; the cut is 'mostly the higher-priced 8i Max', so this is the low side) = $15.24B of calendar-2027 XPU revenue. Broadcom FY2027 runs Nov 2026-Oct 2027, so Jan-Oct 2027 = 10/12 = $12.70B in FY2027 against the booked FY2027 ai_rev $110,148M = -11.5%. Networking is NOT cut: Kuo describes a mix shift to MediaTek 8t, not less Google compute, so the Ethernet/Tomahawk content around those clusters can stay with Broadcom (if it does not, the cut grows to about -16% with the 0.7457 XPU share gross-up). Screen only (rule 22); the update researches the path. Note for the update: the AVGO set's own text conflicts on which TPU Broadcom designs (one row says Broadcom's TPUs are 8t per Tom's Hardware, another that Broadcom ships 8i); Kuo names Broadcom as the 8i designer and MediaTek as 8t.
moves.item: Ming-Chi Kuo survey: Google cuts 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU 8i shipments ~1M units (~20% of 2027 8i), shifts toward MediaTek-designed TPU 8t
